title: Mapping the Phase Space of Cubic Chiral Semiconductors: High-Throughput Search,Stability, and Prototype Families
summary: A high-throughput computational search of 24,227 cubic chiral structures identified 368 candidates on the computed convex hull and 3,048 within 50 meV/atom. Selected candidates were refined with density-functional theory, and several prototype families showed computed intermediate-band features. This is a computational candidate set, not experimental synthesis.
ai_technology: M3GNet relaxed randomly generated structures and ALIGNN predicted convex-hull distances to screen candidates before DFT refinement.
organization: University of Liverpool; University of Cambridge

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; first result-bearing version and date verified from primary record.

evidence.tested: M3GNet geometry relaxation and ALIGNN screening were followed by DFT refinement; ALIGNN hull-distance predictions were evaluated on a holdout set with 33 meV/atom mean absolute error.
evidence.unknown: Predicted stability and electronic structures have not been confirmed by synthesis; results depend on computational approximations.
